volume.title: A Widow's Reckoning
volume.cover: A small calf-bound book. The sums of a household run between survey bearings; a child has drawn boots on every triangle.
volume.index: The widow copied a traveller's bearings into her accounts.
volume.proof: Her repeated subtraction encodes an older place-name. The household sums remain household sums; there is no miracle in the page.

volume.title: The Surveyor Who Would Not Come Home
volume.cover: A rain-swollen folio of bearings, letters and increasingly furious corrections in another hand.
volume.index: A letter gives the surveyor's last reliable itinerary.
volume.proof: The corrections agree on one invariant. It restores the designation beneath the surveyor's mistaken spelling, not a command for operating what lies there.

volume.title: Tables for an Unfinished Stair
volume.cover: Antique load tables, a plan of lodgings and a recipe for onion soup. Several pages were once used to pack a lens.
volume.index: A maintenance itinerary survives beside the soup recipe.
volume.proof: The loads were recorded in paired measures. Translating the ratio restores the name in the maintenance register.

volume.title: Instructions for a Funeral That Did Not Happen
volume.cover: A stitched book of mourning customs. Its endpapers are recycled survey sheets, stamped and annotated in a much older hand.
volume.index: The recycled sheet preserves a route to the survey's source.
volume.proof: The endpaper's coordinate transformation preserves orientation. It identifies the source's older name. The funeral instructions have nothing to say about other planes.

volume.title: The Little Book of Bad Instruments
volume.cover: An old apprentice drew dividers, water-clocks and broken sighting arms here. The masters blamed the weather for every crooked line.
volume.index: One master's journey is recorded between calibration failures.
volume.proof: A correction shared by the surviving instruments restores the place-name in their service record. It is calibration, not sorcery.
